sections.h2: What should a Menifee County homeowner know about property tax?
sections.html:
Menifee County property tax is set and collected by three separate offices in Frenchburg: the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values the house, the sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the county clerk takes over any bill left unpaid after April 15. A seller who knows which office holds which piece can settle a bill or correct a value quickly.

The county site lists the PVA, clerk and county attorney at 12 Main Street, while the sheriff keeps a separate post office box. Treat each as its own contact when you plan a sale.

sections.h2: What is Menifee County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Menifee County is a mountain county of about 204 square miles of land, formed on May 29, 1869 from parts of Bath, Montgomery, Morgan, Powell and Wolfe counties. Frenchburg is the seat and the only city, and the county site says it was incorporated in 1871. The county sits in the foothills of the Cumberland Plateau, between Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge, and it is less than 70 miles east of Lexington by the Mountain Parkway.

Much of the land lies in the Daniel Boone National Forest, and only about 10 percent is cultivated farmland. That shapes what is for sale: hillside homes, small tracts, and cabins that draw visitors. The county website names tourism, forestry, small business, agriculture and public service as the local economy.

Weather has left a mark on the housing stock. An EF3 tornado crossed Menifee and nearby counties on March 2, 2012, and three people were killed across the affected counties. A buyer or lender may ask about storm repairs on an older house, so keep receipts and permits together.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Menifee County housing?
sections.html:
The county had 6,113 residents in 2020, down from 6,306 in 2010, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 6,430 is a 5.2 percent rebound. The 2020 count found 3,277 housing units with 24.3 percent of them vacant, and every resident was counted as rural.

The five year survey for 2020 through 2024 describes the market a seller faces:

  • Three in four homes (75.5 percent) are lived in by their owners.
  • Households with a mortgage report median owner costs of $996 a month, and those without one report $299.
  • Only 81.2 percent of households have a broadband subscription, so ask what internet a buyer can get at a remote address.
  • Workers spend a mean 29.8 minutes getting to a job.

sections.h2: Which Menifee County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Each office has a fixed job, and mail goes to a different box for each, so address a payment or an appeal carefully.

  • Sheriff: collects tax bills. P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875.
  • PVA: assessments, exemption forms and conferences. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 36, phone (606) 768-3514.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and the appeal filing desk. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 123, phone (606) 768-3512.
  • County Attorney: notices and payment plans on delinquent bills. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 545, phone (606) 768-2606.

Call ahead for office hours before you drive in.

sections.h2: When are Menifee County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Menifee County follows the Kentucky collection schedule in KRS 134.015: a 2 percent discount through November 1, the plain bill amount from November 2 to December 31, then penalties. The sheriff mails bills in the fall, and the bill reflects whoever owned the property on January 1.

  • Payment in full by November 1: 2 percent off.
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount.
  • January 1 to 31: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty. The Department of Revenue shows a 21 percent total penalty from February 1 to April 15.
  • Close of business April 15: unpaid bills go to the county clerk.

If a house sells after January 1, expect the bill to stay in the previous owner's name for that year. Settle who pays it in the contract, and ask the sheriff for the amount outstanding.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Menifee County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the Menifee County PVA during the May inspection period, then file with the county clerk if you still disagree. The roll opens on the first Monday in May for two weeks, and a filing is due no later than one workday after the period closes.

The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after the inspection period ends, and it can sit no more than five days without state approval. The Department of Revenue says the board denies an appeal that arrives without facts, so bring support for the number you claim.

  • Photos and written estimates for repairs, such as a roof or a failing foundation on a slope.
  • Sales of similar houses in Menifee County over the past year.
  • Insurance papers or construction cost records.

You may record the hearing. A paid representative must fit the categories in KRS 133.120, which the Department of Revenue lists, and must hold written authority from you.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Menifee County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
An owner who is 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled, can claim the exemption on the home where they live by filing with the Menifee County PVA. KRS 132.810 allows one exemption per residential unit, and a mobile home or manufactured house counts as a unit.

The statute ties the dollar amount to the cost of living index and adjusts it every two years when the index moves by at least 1 percent, so ask the PVA for the current figure. A person who qualifies after paying gets a refund of the tax on the exempt amount. When a homestead property is sold or the owner dies, the transfer must be reported to the PVA, and the next owner applies separately.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Menifee County taxes?
sections.html:
After April 15 the sheriff hands the bill to the clerk, who records a lien and starts interest at 1 percent a month. The clerk adds a 10 percent fee, the county attorney adds 20 percent, and the clerk sells certificates to outside buyers beginning in mid-July.

Written notices follow, and a payment plan with the county attorney is possible until a certificate is sold. A purchaser can add substantial fees. Under KRS 134.015 the tax is a personal debt of the person who owned on the assessment date, and the lien can stay on the parcel for 11 years whoever owns it later.

sections.h2: How are cabins and short-term rentals taxed in Menifee County?
sections.html:
The county charges a 4 percent transient tax on short-term rentals, and its Departments page links the registration form and the monthly return. That matters in a county between Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge, where visitors rent cabins.

A buyer who plans to rent a house will want those filings in order. If you rented yours, gather past returns and tell the buyer what you filed. Ask the county tourism office listed on the same page how registration works for a new owner.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Menifee County house that has tax owing?
sections.html:
Yes. An open bill, or one already at the clerk, becomes a payoff figure, and the sheriff or clerk can quote the amount. Interest grows each month once the bill reaches the clerk, so the figure changes from one month to the next.

Many Menifee County homes are inherited, rural or in need of work. Compare a listing with a cash offer by subtracting repairs, carrying costs and any back tax from each. Ask for the payoff in writing before you accept anything.

faqs.q: Whom do I pay for Menifee County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Menifee County Sheriff, P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875. Include the bill number with a mailed payment.

faqs.q: What is the last day to avoid a penalty on a Menifee County bill?
faqs.a: December 31 is the last day to pay the face amount, per the state schedule. A 5 percent penalty applies from January 1 through January 31.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Menifee County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: File with the Menifee County Clerk after a conference with the PVA. The deadline is one workday after the May inspection period closes.

faqs.q: Does Menifee County offer a senior property tax break?
faqs.a: Yes, the Kentucky homestead exemption applies to owners 65 or older who live in the home. Apply at the PVA office at 12 Main Street in Frenchburg.

faqs.q: Can the county take my house over a small unpaid bill?
faqs.a: A lien is recorded on the property after April 15, and collection can include a sale of the certificate to a private buyer. Contact the county attorney early about a payment plan.
